meta.note: These are recommended learning orders, not rigid prerequisites or guaranteed timelines. Students can revisit earlier stages, skip familiar material after demonstrating the skills, or adapt the route to a particular job description. Optional stages are marked in the interface.

Programming Fundamentals.focus: Variables, control flow, functions, collections, files, debugging, tests, and Git basics.
Programming Fundamentals.ready_when: You can build a small program from a blank file, handle a bad input, test a few cases, and explain how it works.
Programming Fundamentals.purpose: Build the coding habits that make later data and AI work easier.

SQL and Database Skills.focus: SELECT and filtering, joins, grouping, constraints, schemas, and query reasoning.
SQL and Database Skills.ready_when: You can answer a practical question with a multi-table query, explain the joins, and check the result for duplicates or missing rows.
SQL and Database Skills.purpose: Learn to retrieve trustworthy information from structured data.

Data Analysis and Storytelling.focus: Data quality, missing values, summaries, exploratory analysis, charts, and clear conclusions.
Data Analysis and Storytelling.ready_when: You can clean a small dataset, produce a meaningful chart, and explain one finding plus one limitation.
Data Analysis and Storytelling.purpose: Learn to understand data before trying to predict or automate with it.

Statistics and Experimentation.focus: Descriptive statistics, probability, uncertainty, sampling, confidence intervals, and experiment design.
Statistics and Experimentation.ready_when: You can explain uncertainty in plain language, choose a reasonable comparison, and identify when a conclusion is not supported.
Statistics and Experimentation.purpose: Build the reasoning needed to evaluate evidence and models responsibly.

AI and Machine Learning.focus: Baselines, train/test splits, regression and classification, suitable metrics, error analysis, and limitations.
AI and Machine Learning.ready_when: You can compare a model with a simple baseline, avoid data leakage, and explain when the result should not be trusted.
AI and Machine Learning.purpose: Move from describing data to building and evaluating predictive systems.

Data Engineering and Pipelines.focus: Data formats, validation, repeatable transformations, rejected-row handling, logging, and automated checks.
Data Engineering and Pipelines.ready_when: Your pipeline can be rerun without creating duplicates, reports invalid records, and has tests for key assumptions.
Data Engineering and Pipelines.purpose: Turn one-off analysis into a dependable data workflow.

Cybersecurity and Risk.focus: Start with networking and operating-system basics, then security fundamentals, threat modelling, defensive triage, and governance.
Cybersecurity and Risk.ready_when: You can explain a defensive finding, identify supporting evidence and uncertainty, and recommend a proportionate next action.
Cybersecurity and Risk.purpose: Learn to reason about systems, evidence, threats, and safe responses.

LLMs and Generative AI.focus: Python and APIs, model behaviour, evaluation, retrieval and grounding, safety, cost, and monitoring.
LLMs and Generative AI.ready_when: You can build a small grounded application, test it with representative questions, inspect failure cases, and document its limits.
LLMs and Generative AI.purpose: Apply generative models to useful tasks while testing reliability, safety, and cost.

Cloud and MLOps.focus: Git and command line, environments and APIs, containers, deployment, monitoring, reproducibility, and rollback basics.
Cloud and MLOps.ready_when: Another person can reproduce your setup, run the service, see useful logs, and understand how failures are handled.
Cloud and MLOps.purpose: Learn to make data and model workflows reproducible and maintainable.

Communication and Data Storytelling.focus: Audience and objective, chart choice, evidence and caveats, short presentations, and feedback.
Communication and Data Storytelling.ready_when: You can explain the problem, evidence, recommendation, and limitation clearly in a short presentation or report.
Communication and Data Storytelling.purpose: Make technical work understandable and useful to the people who need to act on it.

Green and Energy Data.focus: Data basics, energy and climate indicators, time-series analysis, and communicating uncertainty.
Green and Energy Data.ready_when: You can analyse a relevant indicator, state the data's limits, and avoid claiming that correlation proves cause.
Green and Energy Data.purpose: Apply data skills to energy, climate, and sustainability questions.

Programming Fundamentals.title: Start from the beginning
Programming Fundamentals.goal: Build confidence writing and debugging small programs before adding specialised tools.

SQL and Database Skills.title: Learn to work with databases
SQL and Database Skills.goal: Learn coding basics first, then retrieve and combine structured data.

Data Analysis and Storytelling.title: Become a data analyst
Data Analysis and Storytelling.goal: Follow the practical flow from code to querying data, analysis, uncertainty, and communication.

Statistics and Experimentation.title: Build statistical reasoning
Statistics and Experimentation.goal: Start with code and data literacy, then study uncertainty and sound comparisons.

AI and Machine Learning.title: Become ready for machine learning projects
AI and Machine Learning.goal: Learn to code, inspect data, reason about uncertainty, and only then build predictive models.

Data Engineering and Pipelines.title: Build reliable data pipelines
Data Engineering and Pipelines.goal: Move from programming and queries to repeatable, tested data workflows and deployment.

Cybersecurity and Risk.title: Explore cybersecurity and risk
Cybersecurity and Risk.goal: Build basic coding confidence, then learn networking, operating systems, defensive security, and evidence-led response.

LLMs and Generative AI.title: Build useful generative AI applications
LLMs and Generative AI.goal: Learn programming and data/model evaluation first, then build a grounded LLM application and prepare it for deployment.

Cloud and MLOps.title: Move toward cloud and MLOps
Cloud and MLOps.goal: Learn programming, database and pipeline basics, then practise reproducible deployment. The AI/ML step is useful for model-focused MLOps, but can be skipped for a cloud-infrastructure focus.

Communication and Data Storytelling.title: Explain data clearly
Communication and Data Storytelling.goal: Practise analysing evidence first, then communicating findings and limitations to a specific audience.

Green and Energy Data.title: Apply data skills to energy and climate
Green and Energy Data.goal: Build a data foundation, learn to reason about trends and uncertainty, then apply the workflow to energy or climate indicators.
